tag: Episode 16 · The Weight of Direct Wealth
title: The Weight of Direct Wealth

beats.t: Time inside the glass walls was thick as honey. While Yeoni blinked once, Yeongnyangi called their name three times outside.
Don't think too long! Borrow just six minutes and fifty-one seconds, and you're out. Sign with a hoofprint!
The contract the rabbit held out slid through the glass and floated before Yeoni's nose. In the interest column, tiny writing went on without end.
(Six minutes and fifty-one seconds. A little more time than the price of two rolls.)
My lady, read all the way to the end. My contract started out that length, too.
Oh, do be quiet, Hour of the Rabbit customer! Advice from a failed predecessor doesn't qualify for a discount.
Yeoni read the bottom line. Late interest payments require additional collateral. Collateral: the customer's birth hour.
You said you'd fill my hour slot. So in the end, you're planning to take it away.
My, aren't you clever! But if you can't get out now, you'll simply stop here, won't you?
Yeoni. Support your breath. Think after that.
Yeoni lowered their breath beneath their belly. Even in the dense time, one breath settled into its proper place. Their head cleared a little.
(If the trap measures time, I don't have enough. But this island's been strange from the beginning.)
(Six rolls and one order slip weighed the same. This island measures weight, not length.)
Tiger. Does this trap measure time by how many hours it is? Or how much it weighs?
Holding its ledger below the dais, the tiger raised its head. This time, it looked straight at Yeoni.
Weight. The only thing in this vault that measures length is the rabbit's ledger.
Oh, Mr. Vault Keeper! You can't just go spilling trade secrets like that!
Then I'll use this. Nothing borrowed, nothing given.
Yeoni lifted a hoof. Beside the nearly seventy-two hours, the small twelve minutes shimmered. Yeoni separated out only those twelve minutes and placed them on the clock face's scale pan.
[ Time received: 71:41:09 — Weight: 0.3 ] [ Time earned by my own hands: 00:12:00 — Weighing ]
The scale's needle trembled. A little at first, then wildly. It made a full circle and stopped at seventy-two.
The glass wall cracked. The cracks spread like a web, then shattered with a chime, scattering into glittering sand.
I'm out! My twelve minutes weighed the same as seventy-two hours!
Direct Wealth. What you earn by your own hands is heavy. The heaviest thing on this island.
A pig kneading dough broke the vault. I'll bump this island up to three stars.
[ Time earned by my own hands: 00:01:00 remaining ]
Huh? One minute left. Guess it only cost eleven.
What kind of rule is that?! Weight? That's cheating!
The rabbit launched itself from the vent. Its paw aimed not at Yeoni but at the golden egg on the dais.
Yundal thrust out his bare hand. The hole swallowed the entire lump of coins in the rabbit's paw. The rabbit lost its balance in midair.
Urgh... Today's tab is going to be really hard to pay.
A cord swung from the stumbling rabbit's neck. From its end hung a tiny hourglass filled with dawn light.
This? Our Hour of the Rabbit customer's! Come and get it if you want it!
Yundal's hand reached halfway toward the hourglass. Just then, a chunk of stone fell from the cracked ceiling, straight toward Yeoni's head.
Yundal turned his hand. The hole swallowed the stone. In that instant, the rabbit bounded back into the vent.
The weakest is always quick at running away! I'll show you your birth hour again next time!
Mister! You could've grabbed it just now!
I could have. But then your head would have been flattened. Those numbers don't add up.
Enough. This is as far as you go.
The tiger climbed onto the dais. With the golden egg beneath its paw, black water began spreading across the floor again.
Take her day. That was the rabbit's share. But not the egg. That's in my ledger.
You said that egg was my character. Why is my character in your ledger?
Because I got into the empty house first.
Yeoni is not empty.
The whole vault shook. Something collapsed upstairs. The machines stopped, and the workers' screams traveled down the corridors.
Breaking the trap has brought the levels down! The people on the first level are getting trapped!
(The factory. That child.)
Yeoni looked once at the egg. Once at the tiger. Then they turned and ran toward the lift rope.
Pig! What about the egg?
Later! There are people upstairs!
The first-level factory tilted. Sand poured between the machines like waterfalls. Luna and Moka were pushing the workers toward the narrow door.
You're late, pig! But I kept her day safe. Nice and warm against my chest.
The panda braced a leaning machine with its broad back. Workers filed out beneath it, skewers still in their mouths.
Yeoni! That little kid won't come out! They say they still have a minute left!
The baby rabbit with folded ears sat in front of a stopped machine. The wrist numbers had not changed. Debt remaining before home: 00:01:00.
Hey, little one. Let's go. This place is collapsing.
The child shook their head. If they left a debt behind, their mother's door would not open. Instead of crying, they clung to the machine.
(My one minute. This time, truly the last minute.)
Yeoni looked down at their hoof. One small line of writing blinked. The last fragment of the twelve minutes they had wanted to frame.
Yeoni touched their hoof to the child's wrist. Tick. The tiniest sound.
[ Flower Pig → Baby Rabbit: 00:01:00 ]  [ Debt remaining before home: 00:00:00 ]
There. Go home now. Take your skewer with you.
For the first time, the child's blurred face became clear. Clutching the skewer, the child ran toward the light beyond the narrow door.
Pig, you just broke your frame. The one inside your heart.
That's okay. The frame's empty, but the nail's still there. I can earn more.
The black tiger stood in the shadow of a collapsed machine, the golden egg in its mouth. Its face said it had heard that tiny tick.
Stupid pig. That minute could have paid off a line or so in your ledger.
I write my own ledger. And I decide where my last minute goes.
The tiger said nothing for a long time. Then the egg in its mouth made a tiny but unmistakable cracking sound.
The egg broke. A palm-sized, ocher dragon crawled between the shell fragments, slipped from the tiger's mouth, and landed on Yeoni's hoof.
A dragon. A baby dragon!
It was my egg. Written in my ledger. Why is it going to you?
Chen Earth is a storehouse. A storehouse sides with the one who gives things out, not the one who piles them up. That's what my teacher said.
The baby dragon curled up on the clock pattern at Yeoni's wrist. The pattern melted away, and a single character engraved itself in its place.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  5/8
辰. Chen. The fifth character.
The tiger closed its empty mouth. It opened the ledger, looked at one line, then shut it again without writing anything.
Uncollected today. Next time, I collect everything.
The black cloak disappeared into the shadow of the fallen machine. Only a piece of eggshell on the floor remained warm.
Dawn. The island's sun caught on the tip of a clock tower hand. In the bakery attic, Moka carefully took the hourglass from his chest.
When it touched Luna's sister's chest, the sand flowed backward into her. Color slowly returned to her faded face.
Luna...? Why are you crying? We need to make the morning dough.
You idiot, Sis! Never sell a day again! Promise me!
I promise. And for today, I think I'll ask customers to pay for their bread with stories instead of time.
I like that. Stories taste like dough before it's baked.
Murmurs rose from the square outside. The people from the factory studied their wrists and looked at one another's faces.
The blurred faces grew clearer little by little. With a skewer in its mouth, the panda bowed to the bakery window.
See? That's the effect of my skewers. Half pig effect, too.
I think this island can have four stars now.
Mister. We missed your birth hour, but come with us. We're bound to meet that rabbit again.
My lady, you just asked me to come with you, didn't you? I'll take that as a sign we're compatible.
Don't believe that's the whole story. Just use it as a guide when choosing your path.
There goes Mr. Cat's jealousy again. All right, I'll come as your guide. A guide who's wandered all four skies.
Then I'll stop calling you mister. I'll call you Yundal. Yundal.
For a moment, Yundal lost his words. Apparently, it had been three years since someone had spoken that alias with a smile.
Yes. Today, I'll go by that name.
Yeongnyangi discreetly hid his left paw behind his back. Yundal's eyes followed it, then returned to Yeoni without a word.
Just then, the baby dragon sneezed. Along with eggshell crumbs, an old sheet of paper shot from its nostrils. It was a library borrowing card.
[ Library of Resources · Borrowing record — Flower Pig: The First Spring · Not returned ]
The First Spring? I've never borrowed a book like that.
That's where memories become books. If a book you've never borrowed is checked out to you, it's a book you've forgotten, my lady.
